standard.title: Specialist vocabulary and word history
standard.description: Understand how vocabulary is used to express greater precision of meaning, including through the use of specialist and technical terms, and explore the history of words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can expand vocabulary by exploring synonyms and antonyms, and using words in context (AC9E4LA11). They have not yet examined how specialist and technical vocabulary achieves precision beyond synonymy, or how word origins (Greek, Latin roots) explain and extend vocabulary.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how specialist and technical vocabulary expresses greater precision than general vocabulary, and use knowledge of word origins including Greek and Latin roots to interpret and extend vocabulary.

nodes.label: Precision through specialist vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why specialist or technical vocabulary expresses more precise meaning than general vocabulary, using examples from at least one learning area.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare a specialist term (e.g. 'humpback whale') with a general term (e.g. 'mammal') in context, and explain what precision is gained by using the specialist term.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse examples of specialist and general vocabulary across at least two learning areas, explaining in each case what the specialist term communicates that the general term does not. Discuss why precision matters in technical or informational contexts.
wider: Examine how the same concept is named differently in everyday vs. specialist discourse (e.g. 'heart attack' vs. 'myocardial infarction') and discuss why specialists choose their vocabulary and what that signals about audience
Collect specialist vocabulary from a learning area text being studied and map the precision it provides — explaining how the specialist lexis builds the field's way of knowing
success_criteria: Explains what a specialist term communicates that a general term does not, using a specific example.
Identifies at least two specialist terms in a learning area text and explains the precision each provides.

nodes.label: Word origins: Greek and Latin roots
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify Greek and Latin roots in common words and use root meaning to interpret unfamiliar vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the meaning of at least two Greek or Latin roots and use that knowledge to explain the meaning of words containing those roots.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain the meaning of a range of Greek and Latin roots encountered in curriculum vocabulary, and use root knowledge to interpret unfamiliar words in context. Apply this to words across multiple learning areas.
wider: Explore how Greek and Latin roots cluster in specific learning area vocabulary (e.g. Greek roots in science and mathematics, Latin roots in law and formal writing) and discuss what this historical pattern reveals
Investigate how compound words built from roots create precise technical meaning (e.g. 'telescope', 'biology') and explore extending this pattern to create new coinages for invented concepts

response_modes.reason: Root knowledge is a vocabulary tool that grows in value as students accumulate more roots. No single root is a hinge; the goal is building a working repertoire of roots encountered across learning areas. Regular encounter and application — rather than deep analysis of a few roots — is the investment signal here.

success_criteria: Identifies the root meaning in at least two unfamiliar words and uses it to explain the word's meaning.
Demonstrates root knowledge transfer — can interpret a word containing a known root encountered in a new context.

nodes.label: Word history shapes meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how a word's history — its origins and etymology — illuminates its current meaning or usage, and connect word history to vocabulary precision.
nodes.minimum_width: Explore the history of at least two words and explain how their origins contribute to understanding their current meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Explore the history of words from different origins — including Greek, Latin, and other language sources — and explain how etymology illuminates precision and meaning. Connect word history to why words are used as they are in specialist contexts.
wider: Research words that have entered English from Australian Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages (e.g. boomerang, kangaroo, billabong) and discuss what their presence in English reveals about cultural contact and knowledge transfer

Explore how the same concept is named through different etymological pathways in different specialist fields (e.g. same structure named from Greek in medicine vs. Latin in botany) and discuss what this reveals about the history of each discipline

response_modes.reason: Word history often feels disconnected from current meaning to students. Encountering etymology across multiple word types — including words from First Nations Australian languages and other non-European sources — helps students see word history as living and purposeful rather than as trivia about the past.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The history of words as a window into precision, cultural contact, disciplinary history, and knowledge transfer is genuinely rich. First Nations Australian word contributions to English, alongside Greek/Latin specialist vocabulary, offer substantive investigation opportunities within year band.
success_criteria: Explains how a word's history illuminates its current meaning with a specific example.
Connects etymology to precision — explains why a word from a particular origin expresses meaning in the way it does.
